identity.title: Benchmarking at the Edge of Comprehension

problem.claim: As frontier LLMs rapidly saturate benchmarks, humans may struggle to create discriminative tasks, supply ground truth, and evaluate complex answers, threatening AI progress measurement.

gap.claim: Standard benchmarking depends on levels of human understanding that may become infeasible in a post-comprehension regime.

contributions.claim: Proposes Critique-Resilient Benchmarking, an adversarial framework for comparing models when full human understanding is infeasible.
Defines critique-resilient correctness: an answer counts as correct when no adversary has convincingly disproved it, with humans acting as bounded verifiers of localized claims.
Uses an itemized bipartite Bradley-Terry model to jointly rank models on solving difficult tasks and generating difficult yet solvable questions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their framework from standard benchmarking by recasting evaluation as adversarial generation-evaluation with bounded human verification and final adjudication.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a mathematical-domain demonstration across eight frontier LLMs in which resulting scores were stable and correlated with external capability measures.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rapid benchmark saturation creates a potential crisis for human task construction, ground-truth provision, and complex-solution evaluation.
The abstract names this challenge the post-comprehension regime.
The proposed framework uses adversarial critique-resilient correctness and localized human verification.
A bipartite Bradley-Terry model jointly ranks solving and question-generation abilities; the method is demonstrated on eight frontier LLMs in mathematics.
Benchmarking is presented as an adversarial generation-evaluation game with humans as final adjudicators.

source_observation.claim: The framework decomposes evaluation into localized claims checked by bounded verifiers rather than requiring complete human comprehension of each task.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests a way to align an ambitious evaluation claim with a narrower, inspectable verification unit.
lessons.application: When proposing evaluation beyond human expertise, define correctness through adversarially contestable subclaims and specify who adjudicates unresolved disputes.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when localized claims cannot represent the target capability or when adversarial proof is itself too difficult to assess.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the external capability measures, stability statistics, baselines, task construction procedure, or adjudication protocol.
It does not establish that critique-resilient scores are valid, reproducible, or causally related to capability; only author-reported stability and correlation are given.
